candidates.source_name: CBCG – Registar banaka (Register of banks)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative enumeration of every licensed bank in Montenegro. Each bank is a buyer of POS/ATM/card-personalisation/software and most run their own tender or 'javni poziv' pages; this register defines the buyer population that other A2 cells must then mine individually.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off HTML scrape / manual extraction into an actor master-list; re-check quarterly for licence additions and withdrawals.
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Registri (payment-system registers hub page)
candidates.why_relevant: Hub page confirmed to link four separate registers (payment systems, payment institutions + agents, e-money institutions + agents, revoked authorisations). Single best snowball entry point for the licensed-payments actor population in ME.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch hub, follow the four child URLs, extract entity tables; schedule quarterly diff to catch new PI/EMI licences.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search then direct fetch of hub page (link list read from page)
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata
candidates.why_relevant: Full list of licensed payment institutions and their agents — the non-bank acquirer/PSP layer that buys terminals, gateways and fiscalisation-compliant POS software. Names here become the seed set for company-level tender and contract-award searches.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape table / download attached PDF-XLS if present; normalise entity names + registration numbers for cross-matching against CRPS and the procurement portal.
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata
candidates.why_relevant: E-money institution register: identifies fintech/EMI actors likely to procure card issuing, KYC, tokenisation and terminal services. Small population, high signal for a payments-vendor market map.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Same scrape pipeline as the PI register; quarterly diff.
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje
candidates.why_relevant: Negative-list companion register (revoked authorisations). Prevents chasing dead actors and flags market exits — useful for dating changes in the buyer population between snapshots.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Low-frequency scrape; join to the positive registers as a status flag.
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Registar platnih sistema
candidates.why_relevant: Enumerates the licensed payment systems/operators in ME. Payment-system operators are direct buyers of switching, clearing and settlement infrastructure — a small but high-value tender-issuing population.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off scrape; link operators to CBCG DNS/RTGS system pages for scheme context.
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Centralni registar transakcionih računa pravnih lica i preduzetnika
candidates.why_relevant: Central register of legal-entity transaction accounts: maps which company banks with which bank. Reveals-indirectly the bank–corporate relationship graph and confirms a legal entity's existence/identifiers for entity resolution against tender award notices.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Targeted lookups only (query-by-entity), not bulk harvesting; use for entity resolution rather than enumeration.
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak banaka

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Pretraga blokiranih pravnih lica i preduzetnika (blocked-accounts search)
candidates.why_relevant: Blocked-account / enforced-collection search. Financial-distress screen on bidders and awardees appearing in procurement records; also a due-diligence pointer when assessing local partners or competitors.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query-by-entity lookups on demand; no bulk crawl.
queries_used: Centralna banka Crne Gore registar platnih institucija spisak banaka

candidates.source_name: CRPS – Centralni registar privrednih subjekata (public search)
candidates.why_relevant: The master company register of Montenegro (legal form, status, founding date, legal representatives). This is the backbone for resolving bidder/awardee names found in tender notices into real legal entities, and for enumerating vendors by activity code.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Form-driven lookups keyed on company name/PIB from award notices; rate-limited. Note it is served over HTTP — check for an HTTPS or newer portal before building a pipeline.
queries_used: CRPS Crna Gora centralni registar privrednih subjekata pretraga

candidates.source_name: eFirma / CRPS portal (Uprava prihoda i carina)
candidates.why_relevant: The tax-administration-hosted face of CRPS, used for e-registration of companies and for accessing company records including beneficial ownership. Alternative access path if pretraga.crps.me is unstable; also documents the registration obligation for foreign software vendors selling into ME.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/assisted lookups; treat as fallback mirror of CRPS.
queries_used: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore registar poreskih obveznika e-fakture spisak

candidates.source_name: Registar stvarnih vlasnika (Beneficial ownership register, within CRPS)
candidates.why_relevant: Beneficial-ownership register built into CRPS (operational since Aug 2021, 25% threshold, AML law basis). Exposes who actually controls local POS/IT integrators and bidders — essential for detecting that several 'independent' bidders share an owner, and for group-level competitor mapping.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Entity-level lookups via CRPS/eFirma; capture UBO names into the actor graph. Verify current access rules (some jurisdictions restricted UBO access after 2022 EU case law).
queries_used: Crna Gora registar stvarnih vlasnika CRPS beneficial ownership register

candidates.source_name: CEJN / ESJN – Elektronski sistem javnih nabavki (registered-bidder and contracting-authority registry)
candidates.why_relevant: The national e-procurement system. Beyond live notices (other cells' job), it maintains the registry of registered economic operators (ponuđači) and the roster of contracting authorities (naručioci) — i.e. the enumerable buyer and bidder populations for the whole A2 workstream.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate contracting authorities and registered suppliers from the system's browse/filter views; check for an API or bulk export before scraping. Registration may be needed for full visibility.
queries_used: CJN Uprava za javne nabavke Crna Gora registar ponuđača portal javnih nabavki obveznici
cejn.gov.me elektronski sistem javnih nabavki Crna Gora registar naručilaca

candidates.source_name: Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki (Ministry of Finance) – ujn.gov.me
candidates.why_relevant: Policy owner for public procurement; publishes the legal definition of who counts as a contracting authority (javni i sektorski naručioci), guidance, registration instructions and annual procurement reports. The annual reports themselves are pointer assets listing buyers and their spend.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl publications/reports section; extract lists of contracting authorities and any published supplier registries as PDF/XLS.
queries_used: CJN Uprava za javne nabavke Crna Gora registar ponuđača portal javnih nabavki obveznici

candidates.source_name: AZZK – Agencija za zaštitu konkurencije: registri dodijeljene državne pomoći i pomoći male vrijednosti
candidates.why_relevant: Operates the state-aid register and de-minimis register (aid granter, beneficiary, measure, decision number, sector, amount, date) plus the annual state-aid report. Directly names companies receiving public money — a complementary enumeration of publicly-funded actors alongside procurement awards.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest annual state-aid reports (PDF) for beneficiary tables; note AZZK published a 2026 notice that access to the two registers requires a submitted access request, so the live register itself may be credentialled.
queries_used: Crna Gora registar dodijeljene državne pomoći Ministarstvo finansija izvještaj o dodijeljenoj državnoj pomoći
candidates.observed_blocker: AZZK notice (Jan 2026) states users must submit a request for access to the state-aid and de-minimis registers; the registers themselves appear not to be openly browsable. Unverified — public report PDFs remain open.

candidates.source_name: Poreska uprava / Uprava prihoda i carina – elektronska fiskalizacija programme pages (software-producer registration)
candidates.why_relevant: The fiscalisation authority publishes technical/functional specifications, software-development instructions, testing timelines and the procedure by which software producers register — the mechanism that in practice creates the list of fiscalisation-approved POS/ENU vendors, i.e. the terminal supply chain map. Highest-value pointer for this cell if the vendor list is published.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the efiskalizacija section for 'obavještenja', technical specification documents and any published producer/software list; contact efiskalizacija@tax.gov.me for the register if not published. Confirm the current live domain (tax.gov.me vs a gov.me subsection) before pipelining.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language fiscalisation search; domain inferred from published contact address efiskalizacija@tax.gov.me
queries_used: lista ovlašćenih proizvođača fiskalnih uređaja Crna Gora Poreska uprava elektronska fiskalizacija
Poreska uprava Crne Gore efiskalizacija tehničke specifikacije softver ENU proizvođači registar
candidates.observed_blocker: URL is inferred from the official e-mail domain, not from a search-result link; treat as unverified.

candidates.source_name: Vendor self-declaration cluster of Montenegrin fiscalisation software providers (fiskalnakasa.me, v2-bit.me, tiramisuerp.com, e-invoices.online)
candidates.why_relevant: In the absence of an openly published approved-vendor register, the vendors who market fiscalisation/POS software in ME self-identify on their own sites. Snowballing these pages reconstructs a de-facto supply-chain map (who integrates with the tax authority, who resells terminals) and yields competitor names for A2 bidder analysis.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Seeded crawl + periodic local-language re-search on 'elektronska fiskalizacija Crna Gora softver'; treat all claims as vendor marketing, cross-check each firm against CRPS.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language fiscalisation search, snowballed to vendor sites
queries_used: lista ovlašćenih proizvođača fiskalnih uređaja Crna Gora Poreska uprava elektronska fiskalizacija

candidates.source_name: Pošta Crne Gore – elektronska fiskalizacija service page
candidates.why_relevant: State postal operator offering fiscalisation e-services — evidence that a large state-owned enterprise acts as both a fiscalisation intermediary and a major procurer of POS/e-service infrastructure. Points to a buyer whose own tender pages should be mined.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Add Pošta CG to the buyer master-list; monitor its own tender/javne nabavke section separately.
queries_used: lista ovlašćenih proizvođača fiskalnih uređaja Crna Gora Poreska uprava elektronska fiskalizacija

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT – Statistički biznis registar (Statistical Business Register)
candidates.why_relevant: Statistical register covering all active business entities, with methodology and periodic 'Broj i struktura poslovnih subjekata' releases. Gives the denominator (how many firms, by NACE sector and size) for sizing the addressable buyer/vendor population that the individual registers enumerate by name.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Download the annual PDF releases and the SBR methodology; annual cadence.
queries_used: MONSTAT statistički poslovni registar Crna Gora preduzeća baza

candidates.source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore (SCMN) – registri licenciranih subjekata
candidates.why_relevant: Capital-market regulator maintaining registers of management companies, investment funds and investment-service licences (including authorised credit institutions). Completes the licensed-financial-actor population beyond banks/PI/EMI; these entities also procure trading, custody and reporting systems.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Locate the 'registri' section and scrape entity tables; semi-annual refresh.
queries_used: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore registar licenciranih subjekata Agencija za nadzor osiguranja registar društava

candidates.source_name: CBCG – Državne institucije / korisni linkovi (directory of Montenegrin state institutions)
candidates.why_relevant: Curated link directory of Montenegrin state institutions maintained by the central bank. Cheap, authoritative snowball asset for discovering further regulators, agencies and contracting authorities (and hence more tender pages) that generic search misses.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Single fetch, extract all outbound links, feed each institution into the per-buyer tender-page discovery pipeline.
queries_used: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore registar licenciranih subjekata Agencija za nadzor osiguranja registar društava

candidates.source_name: Privredna komora Crne Gore (Chamber of Economy) – member/association structures
candidates.why_relevant: Chamber of Economy organises members into sector boards (odbori/udruženja) including ICT. Membership and board listings surface the local integrator/vendor population that bids on bank and public POS tenders, and the chamber also republishes procurement and state-aid legislation.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl sector-board (odbor/udruženje) pages and event/participant lists for company names; cross-match to CRPS. No confirmed searchable member directory was found — verify before assuming one exists.

candidates.source_name: DRI – Državna revizorska institucija (State Audit Institution) audit reports on registers and budget execution
candidates.why_relevant: The state auditor has audited CRPS management directly ('Efikasnost upravljanja jedinstvenim registrom privrednih subjekata') and audits budget execution. These reports reveal how complete/reliable each register actually is and name spending units — a rare independent quality assessment of our pointer assets.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest performance-audit PDFs; use them to grade the reliability of CRPS and other registers before relying on them.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from state-aid and CRPS searches

negative_findings.description: No openly published 'lista ovlašćenih proizvođača fiskalnih uređaja' / approved fiscalisation-software-producer list was located for Montenegro, despite targeted local-language searching. Sources confirm a registration procedure for software producers exists (with the tax authority publishing instructions and a contact address efiskalizacija@tax.gov.me) but no public roster surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two sr-language searches returned only vendor marketing pages and employer-association explainers; no official vendor list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This was the single highest-value pointer in the cell rationale — it would map the entire POS/terminal supply chain in one document. Its absence means the supply-chain map must be reconstructed indirectly from vendor self-declaration plus procurement award notices.

negative_findings.description: AZZK published a notice (dated Jan 2026) that access to the register of granted state aid and the de-minimis register requires a submitted access request, indicating the registers are not openly browsable even though annual aggregate reports are public.
negative_findings.result_summary: Register likely gated; annual state-aid reports (e.g. EUR 2.87m granted in 2025) remain public via AZZK and press.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Beneficiary-level state-aid data would complement award notices; if gated, we fall back to annual report PDFs at lower granularity.

negative_findings.description: No searchable member directory (imenik članova) was found for the Chamber of Economy of Montenegro; searches surfaced only governance pages, contacts and social media.
negative_findings.result_summary: komora.me appears to lack an open member-search facility.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Chamber directories are usually a cheap vendor-enumeration shortcut; here the ICT vendor population must instead be derived from CRPS activity codes and procurement bidder lists.

negative_findings.description: The CRPS public search and several CRPS content pages are served over plain HTTP (http://www.pretraga.crps.me/, http://crps.me/strana/pregled/NN) with an id-based URL scheme, alongside a parallel tax-administration portal (efirma.tax.gov.me). Which of the three is the canonical, maintained front end is unclear.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three overlapping CRPS front ends observed; none confirmed canonical.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collection pipeline built on the wrong host risks silent breakage; the numeric /strana/pregled/NN paths are also likely to shift.

negative_findings.description: The tax authority's fiscalisation programme URL was inferred from the official contact address domain (tax.gov.me) rather than from a search-result link; the institution has also been renamed/merged into 'Uprava prihoda i carina', so content may now sit under gov.me.
negative_findings.result_summary: No direct search hit on an official efiskalizacija landing page.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The authoritative fiscalisation vendor and specification documents are the cell's key asset; the entry point must be pinned down before monitoring is set up.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching for Montenegrin registers returns mostly commercial aggregators and wikipedia rather than the registers themselves; substantive discovery in this cell was only possible in Serbian/Montenegrin.
negative_findings.result_summary: English queries produced low-value results; sr queries produced all authoritative hits.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms local-language collection is mandatory for ME A2, and that any monitoring keyword set must be built from sr terms (registar, spisak, pretraga, ponuđač, naručilac, javne nabavke).

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed public list of fiscalisation-approved POS/ENU device and software vendors was located, so the terminal supply chain remains unenumerated at the authoritative level.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the tax authority (Uprava prihoda i carina) fiscalisation section directly and, if nothing is published, send a freedom-of-information / direct request to efiskalizacija@tax.gov.me for the register of registered software producers.

coverage_gaps.description: The roster of contracting authorities (naručioci) — public and sectoral — was not extracted; only the legal definition and the registration mechanism were confirmed. Municipalities and state-owned enterprises (Pošta CG, utilities) are likely a large share of POS-adjacent demand.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Log in / browse CEJN (cejn.gov.me) and the ujn.gov.me annual reports to extract the full naručilac list into the buyer master-table, then hand it to the notice-monitoring cells.

coverage_gaps.description: Insurance supervision (Agencija za nadzor osiguranja) and microcredit/leasing institution registers were referenced conceptually via CBCG's financial-system pages but no specific register URL was confirmed for the insurance supervisor.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/finansijska-stabilnost/finansijski-sistem-crne-gore and the state-institutions link directory to resolve the insurance supervisor's current name, domain and register URLs.

coverage_gaps.description: None of the identified registers were confirmed to offer an API, bulk export or open-data dump; all appear to be HTML pages or form-driven search.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check data.gov.me (Montenegrin open-data portal) for machine-readable copies of CRPS, procurement and state-aid data before committing to scrapers.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level pointer assets that would list Montenegrin buyers and awards (TED, EU IPA-funded contract award databases, EBRD/World Bank procurement notice archives) were not covered in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign a follow-up pass to IFI/EU procurement archives, which frequently fund Montenegrin banking-sector and fiscalisation IT projects and publish awarded-supplier names.

brief: Montenegro's pointer layer for A2 is unusually well-formed on the financial-regulator side: CBCG publishes a compact set of official registers (banks; payment systems; payment institutions and agents; e-money institutions and agents; plus a revoked-authorisation negative list), and CRPS — reachable via pretraga.crps.me, crps.me and efirma.tax.gov.me — is the master company register, now carrying the beneficial-ownership register inside it since 2021. On the procurement side the enumerable populations exist but sit behind the CEJN/ESJN e-procurement system (registered ponuđači and the naručilac roster) with ujn.gov.me as the policy and reporting front end; AZZK holds the state-aid and de-minimis registers but appears to gate them behind an access request. The critical miss is fiscalisation: no public list of approved fiscal-device/POS software producers surfaced despite mandatory local-language searching, so the terminal supply chain currently has to be reconstructed indirectly from vendor self-declaration sites plus procurement awards — closing that gap by going directly to the tax authority should be the next action for this cell.
